phrases.translation: Alif-Lãm-Ra. These are the verses of the clear Book
phrases.explanation: The separate letters are left by many early commentators to the knowledge of Allah while still recited as revelation. What follows is called the clear Book, a description that suits a chapter told largely as one continuous story. Clarity here does not mean the events are simple. It means the listener can follow the hand of God through dream, pit, prison, and palace without losing the road.

phrases.translation: Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Quran so that you may understand
phrases.explanation: An Arabic Quran sent down so that you may understand joins language with responsibility. The first audience receives the message in its own tongue, so the story cannot be dismissed as foreign sounds needing a priestly key before conscience can move. Understanding in this chapter will happen through narrative recognition as much as argument. A family drama carries doctrine about envy, patience, providence, chastity, forgiveness, and power into memorable scenes.

phrases.translation: We relate to you ˹O Prophet˺ the best of stories through Our revelation of this Quran,
phrases.explanation: The best of stories has been understood as the finest narration in truth, benefit, and arrangement, not merely the most entertaining tale. Joseph story gathers a child dream, family jealousy, slavery, temptation, prison, dreams at court, famine administration, and reunion into one arc. Calling it best teaches the audience to measure a story by the wisdom its ending reveals rather than by speed or spectacle alone.

phrases.translation: though before this you were totally unaware ˹of them˺
phrases.explanation: Before revelation Muhammad was unaware of these detailed reports in this form, one of the heedless concerning them. The verse presents the narration as new knowledge given to a man not trained in the scriptures of earlier communities. It also protects the listener from treating the story as tribal folklore polished by a poet. Its authority rests in revelation, while its human scenes remain recognisable in any household.

phrases.translation: ˹Remember˺ when Joseph said to his father, “O my dear father!
phrases.explanation: Joseph begins as a child speaking tenderly to his father, and that closeness matters because the whole plot will turn on the special love between them. My dear father carries affection in the Arabic form echoed by the translation. A dream is being handed to the one person able to read its scale. The story opens at a kitchen table scale before kingdoms and prisons enlarge it.

phrases.translation: Indeed I dreamt of eleven stars, and the sun, and the moon—I saw them prostrating to me!”
phrases.explanation: Eleven stars with sun and moon prostrating gives the child a cosmic family picture he cannot yet interpret. Early reading naturally links the eleven to brothers and the two lights to parents, a meaning fulfilled only near the end. Prostration here signifies honour and submission in greeting according to the customs discussed by commentators, not worship of Joseph. The dream is a seed whose harvest requires decades.

phrases.translation: He replied, “O my dear son! Do not relate your vision to your brothers, or they will devise a plot against you.
phrases.explanation: Jacob tells him not to relate the vision to his brothers because a true report can still be dangerous when envy is listening. Wisdom includes timing and audience, not only accuracy. A father who believes the dream protects it by silence rather than displaying it as a family announcement. The plot they might devise is named before any plot exists, which shows Jacob already reading the emotional weather of his house.

phrases.translation: Surely Satan is a sworn enemy to humankind
phrases.explanation: Satan is a clear enemy to humanity explains how brotherly jealousy can be fanned into crime without reducing the brothers to puppets. An enemy works through suggestion, comparison, and wounded pride, all present before any hand touches Joseph. Naming that enemy helps the child understand that family conflict has a spiritual tempter behind its ordinary sentences. It also teaches readers to guard dreams and blessings from careless exposure.

phrases.translation: And so will your Lord choose you ˹O Joseph˺, and teach you the interpretation of dreams,
phrases.explanation: Your Lord will choose you and teach you the interpretation of events or dreams gives the dream a future skill as well as a future rank. Interpretation will rescue Joseph in prison and Egypt in famine, so the father blessing unknowingly lists the tools of the plot. Choosing here means divine selection for prophethood and service rather than mere family favouritism, a distinction the brothers will struggle to accept.

phrases.translation: and perfect His favour upon you and the descendants of Jacob—
phrases.explanation: Perfecting favour on Joseph and the house of Jacob promises completion rather than a partial glimpse. The family story is headed somewhere even when the next scene places the chosen child in a pit. Perfection of favour can include prophecy, beauty, character, authority, and reunion in early explanation. For the reader, the promise becomes a lamp carried through dark chapters where circumstances appear to contradict it.

phrases.translation: ˹just˺ as He once perfected it upon your forefathers, Abraham and Isaac. Surely your Lord is All-Knowing, All-Wise.”
phrases.explanation: As He perfected it on Abraham and Isaac places Joseph inside a tested lineage rather than a sudden exception. Both forefathers knew delay, danger, family pain, and promises that looked impossible in the middle. All Knowing and All Wise close the father speech because the road from dream to fulfilment will require knowledge no child possesses and wisdom no grieving parent can see whole.

phrases.translation: Indeed, in the story of Joseph and his brothers there are lessons for all who ask
phrases.explanation: In Joseph and his brothers are signs for those who ask tells the audience how to listen. A sign is an event that points beyond itself, so the narrative should not be consumed only for suspense. Askers may be people who requested the story or anyone seeking evidence about God management of a life. Each turn will ask whether the reader can see providence before the ending explains it.

phrases.translation: ˹Remember˺ when they said ˹to one another˺, “Surely Joseph and his brother ˹Benjamin˺ are more beloved to our father than we,
phrases.explanation: The brothers begin with comparative love, naming Joseph and his full brother Benjamin as dearer to their father while they are a strong company. Strength in numbers becomes their imagined claim on affection, as if ten workers should outweigh a child in a father heart. Envy often starts as arithmetic because counting hurts less than admitting a wish to be preferred. Their sentence already turns love into a contested inheritance.

phrases.translation: even though we are a group of so many. Indeed, our father is clearly mistaken
phrases.explanation: Our father is in clear error judges Jacob inner life from the outside and gives the group permission to correct him by crime. Error can carry the sense of being absorbed or mistaken in love rather than theological misguidance in early readings. The brothers do not ask whether a younger motherless child needs special tenderness. A grievance becomes dangerous when it appoints itself judge over the person it resents.

phrases.translation: Kill Joseph or cast him out to some ˹distant˺ land so that our father’s attention will be only ours,
phrases.explanation: Kill Joseph or cast him into a land escalates private envy into two methods of erasure. Murder removes the body while exile removes the presence, and either is expected to clear their father face for themselves alone. Attention imagined as a face turning toward them shows the real prize. They want undivided regard, a thing no crime can manufacture because guilt will stand between them and every future look.

phrases.translation: then after that you may ˹repent and˺ become righteous people!”
phrases.explanation: Then afterward be righteous people reveals a planned repentance attached to a planned sin. They bargain with conscience in advance, promising future goodness as payment for present violence. The chapter will show that repentance is real but not a coupon printed before a crime. Scheduling morality after harm is one of envy most polished tricks, since it allows the heart to feel religious while the hands prepare a pit.

phrases.translation: One of them said, “Do not kill Joseph. But if you must do something,
phrases.explanation: One speaker reduces the plan from killing to the bottom of a well, often identified in reports with the eldest brother, although the Quran leaves him unnamed. His intervention is only a lesser evil, yet inside a group moving toward murder it becomes the crack through which life survives. The story will repeatedly use partial human mercy as an instrument of a larger providence that none of the actors can see.

phrases.translation: throw him into the bottom of a well so perhaps he may be picked up by some travellers.”
phrases.explanation: Some caravan may pick him up completes the alternative with a hope that sounds casual and becomes exact prophecy. A well on a travelled route turns abandonment into transport toward Egypt, although the brothers imagine distance as disappearance. If you must do something exposes group pressure even in the voice of restraint. He cannot yet stop the company, yet his sentence reroutes the entire future of nations.

phrases.translation: They said, “O our father! Why do you not trust us with Joseph, although we truly wish him well
phrases.explanation: Why do you not trust us with Joseph turns the request into a complaint about injured honour. They call themselves sincere advisers or well wishers toward him, language designed to make Jacob caution look insulting. Manipulation often begins by forcing a protective person to defend suspicion instead of discussing the child safety. The brothers have rehearsed innocence before approaching the father, and their question is part of the costume.

phrases.translation: Send him out with us tomorrow so that he may enjoy himself and play.
phrases.explanation: Send him tomorrow to enjoy and play gives the outing the sound of ordinary childhood rather than a removal plot. Eating, roaming, and playing in open land would be good for a boy in normal circumstances. The request uses a true good as cover for a false intention, which is why Jacob discernment matters. Evil plans rarely announce their real itinerary. They borrow the vocabulary of care until the gate closes behind the child.

phrases.translation: And we will really watch over him.”
phrases.explanation: We will guard him becomes the oath on which the plan depends. Ten older brothers present themselves as a wall around the youngest, a plausible claim from their strength. The sentence later returns as bitter evidence because protection was promised by the very hands that lowered him. Readers learn to listen for the gap between capacity and intention, since being able to guard is not the same as willing to.

phrases.translation: He responded, “It would truly sadden me if you took him away with you,
phrases.explanation: Jacob says their taking him grieves him before he mentions any wolf, a detail that exposes attachment without accusing his sons aloud. Separation from Joseph is pain even if the trip ends safely by evening. A wise father can sense a danger he cannot prove. His reply stays diplomatic because direct accusation might harden the brothers or fracture the house before the child can be protected.

phrases.translation: and I fear that a wolf may devour him while you are negligent of him.”
phrases.explanation: I fear a wolf may eat him while you are heedless supplies the brothers with the exact script they will later perform. Heedlessness makes the danger credible without calling them murderers, since a group playing can lose sight of a child. The line is painful in hindsight because protective speech can be mined by plotters. Yet Jacob responsibility is not the same as their guilt, and the story never lets the excuse sound original.

phrases.translation: They said, “If a wolf were to devour him, despite our strong group, then we would certainly be losers!”
phrases.explanation: If a wolf eats him while we are a company we would be losers turns their strength into a public guarantee. Losers here means weak, ruined in honour, and guilty of failed protection rather than a sports result. The brothers use masculine pride to close the discussion because each objection seems to insult the group. Their sentence raises the cost of failure so high that a later lie will need a shirt, blood, and tears to survive.

phrases.translation: And so, when they took him away and decided to throw him into the bottom of the well,
phrases.explanation: When they took him and agreed to place him in the unseen bottom of the well, the narration moves quickly over a child terror. Agreement matters because the crime is collective even if one voice prevented murder. Darkness at the bottom becomes the first fulfilment of the dream in reverse, as the boy promised cosmic honour sits below the feet of his brothers. The story refuses to make providence sentimental.

phrases.translation: We inspired him: “˹One day˺ you will remind them of this deed of theirs while they are unaware ˹of who you are˺.”
phrases.explanation: Revelation to Joseph that he will one day inform them of this act while they do not recognise him gives the child and the reader a future inside the pit. Commentators discussed whether this was prophetic revelation or divine inspiration suited to his state. Either way, comfort arrives as knowledge rather than immediate rescue. God sometimes answers darkness first by telling the sufferer that the story is longer than the present hour.

phrases.translation: Then they returned to their father in the evening, weeping
phrases.explanation: Returning in the evening weeping gives the lie a performance before it has words. Evening lets tears do the work of evidence in dim light, and collective weeping makes each brother borrow credibility from the group. Real grief is present in the house, but it will belong chiefly to the father and the child in the well. The verse teaches that emotion displayed at the right hour is not yet proof.

phrases.translation: They cried, “Our father! We went racing and left Joseph with our belongings, and a wolf devoured him!
phrases.explanation: We went racing and left Joseph with our goods supplies the careless detail needed by Jacob wolf prediction. Racing explains distance and distraction in one stroke, while belongings place the child as an unpaid guard rather than a player. The story has internal logic if heard quickly. On reflection it asks why ten protectors left the smallest boy alone at the exact point their father feared, a crack Jacob sees without needing a court.

phrases.translation: But you will not believe us, no matter how truthful we are.”
phrases.explanation: You will not believe us even if we are truthful anticipates rejection and tries to make it sound like prejudice. Liars often add this sentence to move the conversation from evidence to the listener fairness. It is accidentally honest about their credibility problem because their earlier acting has trained the father not to rest in their tone. Truthfulness becomes a claim they must assert since the facts will not carry it.

phrases.translation: And they brought his shirt, stained with false blood. He responded, “No!
phrases.explanation: False blood on the shirt is stage evidence prepared from an animal, according to the common reports around the passage. Jacob reply begins with no because the shirt itself tells against the tale when its condition is considered in early explanation. A garment can lie when carried by liars, yet it can also testify when read carefully. This shirt is the first of three in the story, each changing a judgment.

phrases.translation: Your souls must have tempted you to do something ˹evil˺.
phrases.explanation: Your souls have made a matter easy for you names the inner negotiation that smoothed the crime before hands acted. Jacob does not specify every detail he suspects, perhaps because proof beyond discernment is unavailable and his sons still stand before him as family. Souls making a thing seem light explains how conscience can be edited by group agreement. The father identifies the source without surrendering to their version.

phrases.translation: So ˹I can only endure with˺ beautiful patience! It is Allah’s help that I seek to bear your claims.”
phrases.explanation: Beautiful patience becomes Jacob programme for a grief without a body or a court remedy. Beautiful patient endurance in early understanding avoids ugly complaint against God while allowing sorrow, tears, and hope to remain. Help is sought from Allah against what they describe, a careful phrase that treats their report as an affliction itself. Instead of erupting, Jacob hands both the missing child and the lying sons to divine custody.

phrases.translation: And there came some travellers, and they sent their water-boy who let down his bucket into the well.
phrases.explanation: A caravan sends its water drawer and a bucket descends into the darkness where the brothers meant the story to stop. Ordinary thirst on a trade road becomes the next divine instrument, without thunder or an army. Joseph rises attached to a bucket, a humiliating and saving image at once. Providence often works through schedules people made for commerce rather than through events labelled miraculous by witnesses.

phrases.translation: He cried out, “Oh, what a great find! Here is a boy!”
phrases.explanation: What good news, here is a boy turns a child into a discovery before anyone asks his name or family. Joy in the water drawer voice may be innocent surprise, commercial excitement, or both. The wording lets readers feel the distance between heaven valuation and market valuation. A future prophet and minister is announced as a found item at a well because slavery has already taught the travellers how to see him.

phrases.translation: And they took him secretly ˹to be sold˺ as merchandise, but Allah is All-Knowing of what they did
phrases.explanation: They conceal him as merchandise while Allah knows what they do interlaces secrecy with perfect observation. Hiding a free child from companions or owners in the caravan serves a quick sale in several early explanations. Merchandise is the saddest word in the verse because it shows how a market can rename a person. God knowledge does not instantly stop the sale, yet it assures readers the chain is being watched and guided.

phrases.translation: They ˹later˺ sold him for a cheap price, just a few silver coins—only wanting to get rid of him
phrases.explanation: A few counted coins and indifference to his value settle Joseph price at the bottom of the market. The sellers want rid of him before questions arise, while the brothers versions sometimes included in reports would make the cheapness a sign of eagerness to disappear the evidence. Either way, heaven chosen child is measured against small silver by men who cannot read a dream. Cheap sale and high destiny travel in the same cart.

phrases.translation: The man from Egypt who bought him said to his wife,
phrases.explanation: The Egyptian who bought him tells his wife to honour his lodging, a courtly command that changes Joseph conditions without ending his slavery. The buyer is identified in tradition as a high official, often called the Aziz, while the Quran keeps the role functional. Kind treatment from a powerful stranger becomes a bridge between well and future authority. A humane impulse inside an unjust system still matters to the person carried by it.

phrases.translation: “Take good care of him, perhaps he may be useful to us or we may adopt him as a son.”
phrases.explanation: Perhaps he will benefit us or we will adopt him as a son gives the household two futures for the slave child, usefulness and family. Adoption language raises the emotional stakes of the later temptation because Joseph will owe gratitude to the master who imagined kinship. Benefit prophecy is larger than the speaker knows. Egypt itself will benefit from the boy at the well when famine makes his interpretation a national resource.

phrases.translation: This is how We established Joseph in the land, so that We might teach him the interpretation of dreams.
phrases.explanation: Thus We established Joseph in the land interprets slavery, sale, and a good master as stages in divine placement. Establishment does not mean he is already powerful. It means the geography of his future has been entered and the education that future needs can begin. Teaching interpretation returns to Jacob words, assuring readers the thread from childhood dream remains unbroken even inside a foreign house.

phrases.translation: Allah’s Will always prevails, but most people do not know
phrases.explanation: Allah prevails over His affair states the theology of the whole story in one sentence. Brothers, merchants, buyers, seducer, prison guards, and kings will all make real choices, yet none can divert the matter God is conducting. Most people do not know because visible causation looks complete to impatient eyes. The verse asks readers to hold two truths together, human guilt remains real and providence is not defeated by it.

phrases.translation: And when he reached maturity, We gave him wisdom and knowledge.
phrases.explanation: When Joseph reached maturity, wisdom and knowledge are given before public office arrives. Growth in a household has formed judgement alongside beauty and dream interpretation in early readings of these gifts. Maturity matters because the next test requires desire to be governed by more than appetite. God preparation is often invisible inside ordinary years, and the verse compresses those years so the reader notices character rather than a birthday.

phrases.translation: This is how We reward the good-doers
phrases.explanation: Thus We reward those who do good beautifully makes Joseph development a pattern rather than a private exception. Excellence in hidden conditions draws gift long before an audience can applaud it. The statement also reassures enslaved and obscure readers that location does not cancel divine education. A bought servant can become a person of wisdom in a house that still calls him property, and heaven notices before Egypt does.

phrases.translation: And the lady, in whose house he lived, tried to seduce him.
phrases.explanation: The woman in whose house he lives seeks to seduce him, reversing the expected script of male power in a slave household. She holds domestic authority while he holds only favour and character. The incident is narrated without voyeurism because the subject is conscience under pressure. Closed doors will remove witnesses, and the story will ask what remains when reputation, gratitude to a master, desire, fear, and God compete in one room.

phrases.translation: She locked the doors ˹firmly˺ and said, “Come to me!”
phrases.explanation: She bolts the doors and says come to me gives the test a single blunt invitation. Bolting can signify layers of privacy in an official residence and her confidence that rank can manage aftermath. No long dialogue is wasted on negotiation because the moral line is clear before she speaks. The chapter uses the room as a second pit, only now the danger arrives as opportunity rather than betrayal by brothers.

phrases.translation: He replied, “Allah is my refuge! It is ˹not right to betray˺ my master,
phrases.explanation: Allah is my refuge begins with an exclamation seeking God protection before any social argument is offered. Refuge language turns the closed room outward toward heaven, as if a door no hand bolted is already present. Joseph names his master favour next in many readings, whether master means Allah, the Egyptian, or both in layered gratitude. Starting with God prevents gratitude to a human benefactor from becoming a polite excuse that might still bend.

phrases.translation: who has taken good care of me. Indeed, the wrongdoers never succeed.”
phrases.explanation: He has made my dwelling good and wrongdoers do not succeed joins gratitude with final outcome. Betraying a kind master in his own house would make Joseph a wrongdoer however private the act stayed. Success is measured at Allah court rather than by escaping the corridor. The sentence is short enough to be remembered by readers in their own closed rooms, where long sermons are rarely available at the needed second.

phrases.translation: She advanced towards him, and he would have done likewise, had he not seen a sign from his Lord.
phrases.explanation: She desired him and he would have desired her had he not seen the proof of his Lord is one of the most discussed sentences in the chapter. Early commentators explored meanings from a passing human inclination checked by prophetic clarity to a conditional statement that he never came near the act. The verse itself centres the proof that turned him away, making divine protection rather than romantic speculation the point for practical reading.

phrases.translation: This is how We kept evil and indecency away from him, for he was truly one of Our chosen servants
phrases.explanation: Thus We turned away evil and indecency because he was among sincere or chosen servants explains the rescue without denying the force of the test. Protection does not always arrive by removing temptation from geography. It can arrive as a sudden clarity inside the tempted person. Sincerity names a prepared relationship with Allah that becomes action at speed. Joseph runs because his heart has somewhere higher to run to.

phrases.translation: They raced for the door and she tore his shirt from the back, only to find her husband at the door.
phrases.explanation: They race to the door and she tears his shirt from behind, turning the private struggle into a public race. The torn garment will become the second shirt of the story and the first clear physical evidence. Her husband at the door arrives at the exact threshold between secret and reputation. A chase that looks chaotic is photographed by providence in cloth, because the direction of a tear can tell who was fleeing.

phrases.translation: She cried, “What is the penalty for someone who tried to violate your wife, except imprisonment or a painful punishment?”
phrases.explanation: What is the penalty for one who intended evil toward your wife except prison or painful punishment is spoken instantly by the guilty woman. She frames the question as if judgment were already settled and only sentencing remained. Accusing first is a familiar strategy when rank believes it can outrun evidence. Prison enters the story through her mouth, ironically naming the place that will preserve Joseph and become his school of public interpretation.

phrases.translation: Joseph responded, “It was she who tried to seduce me.”
phrases.explanation: She sought to seduce me is Joseph whole defence before evidence speaks. He does not embellish, bargain, or expose more than the accusation requires. Brevity becomes a mark of truthfulness in a scene where the woman has already produced a legal theory. A slave against a minister wife has little procedural hope, so the next voice matters as an unexpected mercy inside the household system.

phrases.translation: And a witness from her own family testified: “If his shirt is torn from the front,
phrases.explanation: A witness from her family testifies introduces an investigator whose kinship removes some suspicion of favour toward Joseph. Reports differ over whether the witness was a child miraculously speaking or a wise relative, and the passage can be read with that history held open. The important movement is method. Instead of rank, gender, or volume deciding, a testable condition is proposed that either side can lose.

phrases.translation: then she has told the truth and he is a liar
phrases.explanation: If the shirt is torn from the front she is truthful assumes a man advancing while a woman pushes him away. Clothing damage becomes a map of bodies in motion, an early forensic argument inside a household dispute. The conditional gives the husband a path that does not require humiliating inquiry. Truth is allowed to arrive through fabric because the main witnesses are interested parties and no one else was inside the bolted room.

phrases.translation: But if it is torn from the back, then she has lied and he is truthful.”
phrases.explanation: If torn from behind she has lied and he is truthful completes the test with the result the chase already hinted. A fleeing man pulled backward by a pursuer leaves a different signature from an attacker resisted at the chest. The court is still private and imperfect, yet evidence has interrupted status. The verse lets a torn shirt preach that God can place testimony inside things unable to flatter rank.

phrases.translation: So when her husband saw that Joseph’s shirt was torn from the back,
phrases.explanation: When the husband sees the tear from behind, knowledge enters the house whether reputation wants it or not. His response will show how power often handles truth once truth becomes embarrassing. The shirt has done more for the slave than any patron spoke aloud in the moment. Seeing is described before speaking, which matters because the official can no longer honestly claim uncertainty as his reason for what follows.

phrases.translation: he said ˹to her˺, “This must be ˹an example˺ of the cunning of you ˹women˺! Indeed, your cunning is so shrewd
phrases.explanation: This is of your women cunning and great is your cunning is the husband saying, quoted in scripture rather than offered as a universal doctrine about every woman. It reflects a powerful man generalising to manage a personal scandal while avoiding full justice. The sentence should be read inside his voice and political interest. Collective labels often appear when an individual case is too uncomfortable to judge cleanly.

phrases.translation: O Joseph! Forget about this. And you ˹O wife˺! Seek forgiveness for your sin. It certainly has been your fault.”
phrases.explanation: Joseph, turn away from this and you, woman, seek forgiveness gives private absolution without a public correction of the lie. The master knows Joseph innocence and his wife guilt, yet reputation management wins the day. Forgiveness is rightly directed to God and fault is named, so the response is not pure denial. The incomplete justice matters because a hidden scandal will continue growing until prison and a later confession force daylight into it.

phrases.translation: Some women of the city gossiped, “The Chief Minister’s wife is trying to seduce her slave-boy.
phrases.explanation: Women in the city gossip that the minister wife is seducing her young servant, showing that household secrecy has failed. Their language attacks her more than Joseph, because his refusal makes her desire look humiliating across class lines. Gossip functions as an unofficial court after the real household declines a clear verdict. The story now widens from a bolted room to a whole elite society judging women through reputation.

phrases.translation: Love for him has plagued her heart. Indeed, we see that she is clearly mistaken.”
phrases.explanation: Love has pierced her heart and we see her in clear error mixes fascination with condemnation. The speakers may be sincere moral critics, social rivals, or both, and the next scene will expose their own reaction to Joseph beauty. Clear error repeats the brothers phrase about Jacob, reminding readers how confidently groups label a person from outside. A city can call desire error while still enjoying the entertainment of describing it at length.

phrases.translation: When she heard about their gossip, she invited them and set a banquet for them.
phrases.explanation: When she hears their scheme or gossip, the minister wife answers with a banquet rather than denial. Reclining couches, refined food, and elite guests turn reputation into theatre. She understands her critics well enough to design an experience instead of an argument. The scene warns that powerful people under moral pressure may not seek innocence. They may seek witnesses who can be made to share the temptation.

phrases.translation: She gave each one a knife, then said ˹to Joseph˺, “Come out before them.”
phrases.explanation: Each woman receives a knife for cutting fruit in the common explanation of the banquet, and Joseph is ordered to come out at the chosen moment. His entrance is timed like a performance although he remains a servant with little control over the stage. The knives look innocent as table tools. In a few seconds they will convert private desire into public physical evidence that the hostess can use.

phrases.translation: When they saw him, they were so stunned ˹by his beauty˺ that they cut their hands, and exclaimed, “Good God!
phrases.explanation: They cut their hands and call him no mortal after being overwhelmed by his beauty, a reaction reports amplified across centuries while the Quran keeps the shock concise. Pain unnoticed in the moment pictures attention captured beyond ordinary manners. Good God or far be it from Allah in their exclamation registers astonishment in religious language. Their earlier moral superiority has been interrupted by the same sight they mocked another woman for pursuing.

phrases.translation: This cannot be human; this must be a noble angel!”
phrases.explanation: This is a noble angel completes their attempt to classify beauty outside ordinary humanity. Giving Joseph an angelic label lets the women excuse their reaction as a response to something irresistible, just as magic labels served other audiences. The sentence matters as social evidence for the hostess rather than theology. They have not become righteous. They have become less able to pretend that desire in the house was easy to govern.

phrases.translation: She said, “This is the one for whose love you criticized me!
phrases.explanation: This is the one concerning whom you blamed me lets the hostess collect the room reaction as her defence. She does not deny pursuing him. She presents shared astonishment as if it transfers responsibility from choice to beauty. Public relations replaces repentance once more, only now female witnesses have been recruited into sympathy through an experience designed for that purpose.

phrases.translation: I did try to seduce him but he ˹firmly˺ refused.
phrases.explanation: I sought to seduce him and he held firm is a startling confession that clears Joseph in public while the speaker still refuses repentance. Truth can be used as a weapon when shame has already been lost. Her sentence establishes his innocence beyond the shirt, since the principal accuser now names her own pursuit. Yet confession without turning becomes another form of control, because she immediately converts honesty into a new threat.

phrases.translation: And if he does not do what I order him to, he will certainly be imprisoned and ˹fully˺ disgraced.”
phrases.explanation: If he does not do what I command he will be imprisoned and humbled issues an ultimatum before the same witnesses. Prison changes from her first panicked accusation into a deliberate instrument of coercion. Humiliation matters as much as confinement because Joseph public honour among the women has just risen. Power that cannot purchase consent prepares to punish refusal, making the next verse a prayer about free conscience under state backed desire.

phrases.translation: Joseph prayed, “My Lord! I would rather be in jail than do what they invite me to.
phrases.explanation: Prison is dearer to me than what they call me to sets liberty and purity in an exchange rate the world rarely accepts. Joseph does not romanticise jail. He chooses a place where his body may be confined over a palace where his obedience would be owned. The plural call suggests pressure has widened beyond one woman to the social circle now enlisted around her demand.

phrases.translation: And if You do not turn their cunning away from me, I might yield to them and fall into ignorance.”
phrases.explanation: If You do not turn their scheme from me I may incline and become ignorant admits need for divine protection rather than boasting of invincible will. Joseph knows prolonged negotiation, flattery, threats, and beauty can wear a person down. Ignorant here means acting foolishly against known truth, not lacking information. The prayer teaches that resisting a system may require requesting removal from its daily reach when private refusal is no longer respected.

phrases.translation: So his Lord responded to him, turning their cunning away from him. Surely He is the All-Hearing, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation: His Lord answered and turned their scheme away while still allowing prison to become the route of protection. An answered prayer does not always preserve comfort or reputation in the currency people expect. Hearing and Knowing describe a God who registered the prayer behind palace doors and understood every social pressure around it. Joseph will lose the house, yet the scheme will lose access to his conscience.

phrases.translation: And so it occurred to those in charge, despite seeing all the proofs ˹of his innocence˺, that he should be imprisoned for a while
phrases.explanation: After seeing the signs of innocence it appears good to them to imprison him for a time, one of the most quietly damning sentences in the chapter. Decision makers do not lack evidence. They need a body removed from conversation so a household and a class can recover its story. For a while has no stated legal term, which makes the injustice feel administrative rather than passionate. A society can know and still choose convenience.

phrases.translation: And two other servants went to jail with Joseph. One of them said, “I dreamt I was pressing wine.”
phrases.explanation: Two young men enter prison with Joseph and one dreams of pressing wine for service again. Prison society brings a cupbearer and a Baker from the royal world into the slave prophet cell in the usual explanation. The dream of squeezing grapes or wine concerns work, favour, and a master cup. A place meant to erase Joseph begins supplying exactly the audience through which his gift will reach the king.

phrases.translation: The other said, “I dreamt I was carrying ˹some˺ bread on my head, from which birds were eating.”
phrases.explanation: The other carries bread on his head while birds eat from it, a dream of service turned into exposure and consumption. Bread that should reach a royal table becomes food for creatures above a helpless head. The pair of dreams move in opposite directions, one toward restored service and one toward death. Their occupational symbols make the later interpretation socially exact, because each man dreams in the materials of the job he hopes to recover.

phrases.translation: ˹Then both said,˺ “Tell us their interpretation, for we surely see you as one of the good-doers.”
phrases.explanation: Tell us its interpretation because we see you among the good doers gives Joseph reputation inside prison. Before asking for technique they identify character, suggesting that his conduct toward prisoners has made him a trusted listener. Excellence in a cell can include prayer, kindness, honesty, and attention to frightened men. The verse shows ministry beginning before interpretation, since people ask sacred questions from someone whose goodness they have watched under injustice.

phrases.translation: Joseph replied, “I can even tell you what kind of meal you will be served before you receive it.
phrases.explanation: Food will not come to you as provision before I tell its interpretation creates a short real time window for a lesson before the dreams are answered. Some commentators also linked the phrase to Joseph ability to interpret experiences more broadly, but the scene plainly lets him speak before delivering their outcomes. He is not teasing desperate men. He uses a brief pause to direct their need toward the source of interpretation.

phrases.translation: This ˹knowledge˺ is from what my Lord has taught me.
phrases.explanation: That is from what my Lord taught me refuses personal mystique around the gift. A prisoner who could build influence by appearing naturally clairvoyant gives away the credit at the first opportunity. Teaching by God connects prison interpretation to Jacob childhood promise. It also separates revelation from fortune telling as entertainment, because every answer must lead back to the teacher if it is to benefit the askers beyond curiosity.

phrases.translation: I have shunned the faith of a people who disbelieve in Allah and deny the Hereafter
phrases.explanation: I have left the way of a people who do not believe in Allah and deny the Hereafter gives the source of teaching a moral biography. Joseph knowledge is not presented as a neutral skill that can be detached from worship. Leaving a disbelieving path is active language for a man carried into foreign houses and prisons. His inner address has remained Abrahamic even while his legal address changed from family to slave quarters to cell.

phrases.translation: I follow the faith of my fathers: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
phrases.explanation: I follow the religion of my fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob names a lineage of monotheism rather than ancestor worship. Unlike opponents who cite fathers to protect idols, Joseph cites fathers who point away from themselves toward Allah. Continuity is therefore not automatically blind tradition. The question is what the ancestors handed down. A family can inherit a road to God or a museum of names that blocks the road.

phrases.translation: It is not ˹right˺ for us to associate anything with Allah ˹in worship˺.
phrases.explanation: It is not for us to associate anything with Allah includes the whole prophetic house under one rule. No saint, ancestor, king, angel, or sacred object receives a share in worship. This sentence reaches the two prisoners inside an Egyptian religious world filled with divine ranks. Joseph does not begin with their dreams symbolism because the God who interprets dreams must not be demoted to one specialist among many.

phrases.translation: This is part of Allah’s grace upon us and humanity, but most people are not grateful
phrases.explanation: This is Allah favour on us and on humanity while most people are ungrateful makes monotheism itself the gift, not merely a correct answer about one night. Favour to humanity means guidance is available beyond Joseph family line. Ingratitude appears when a blessing meant to organise life is treated as a curiosity for emergencies. The prisoners wanted a dream decoded. Joseph offers the decoder a face and a claim.

phrases.translation: O my fellow-prisoners! Which is far better: many different lords or Allah—the One, the Supreme
phrases.explanation: O my two companions of prison turns two frightened men into addressed friends rather than specimens. Are many separate lords better or Allah the One and Irresistible uses their experience of hierarchy to ask a governing question. Egypt has shown them masters, jailers, palace ranks, and conflicting powers. One supreme Lord simplifies ultimate loyalty because the highest door is also the final refuge. The argument is tender in address and exact in content.

phrases.translation: Whatever ˹idols˺ you worship instead of Him are mere names which you and your forefathers have made up—a practice Allah has never authorized.
phrases.explanation: What you worship besides Him are only names you and your fathers named returns to fabrication as language without authority. A name can acquire temples, festivals, fear, and ancestry while still lacking a revealed warrant. Joseph challenges the paperwork of polytheism, asking who authorised these titles to receive worship. Fathers appear again, but unlike his own forefathers they function as editors inventing divinity rather than witnesses transmitting it.

phrases.translation: It is only Allah Who decides. He has commanded that you worship none but Him.
phrases.explanation: Judgment belongs only to Allah and He commands worship of none but Him links sovereignty to devotion. In prison, a human court has already Mishandled innocence, so a higher judgment carries emotional force. The God who decides final outcomes is the only being entitled to ultimate obedience. This does not erase earthly law. It reveals its rank and prevents kings, priests, and ancestors from occupying the seat of final command.

phrases.translation: That is the upright faith, but most people do not know
phrases.explanation: That is the upright religion while most people do not know ends the sermon with straightness and an explanation for its rarity. A religion can be upright in content yet unpopular because it removes negotiable gods and local exceptions. Knowing here means more than having heard the sentence. It means letting the One Lord reorganise fear, hope, gratitude, and conduct. Only after this foundation does Joseph interpret the two dreams awaiting life and death.

phrases.translation: “O my fellow-prisoners! ˹The first˺ one of you will serve wine to his master,
phrases.explanation: One of you will pour wine for his lord again turns the cupbearer dream toward restoration in the palace service he lost. Joseph does not soften the difference between the two outcomes by assigning names in the sentence, although each man can hear his own dream. Occupational hope becomes a verdict. A prisoner skilled in interpretation is also asked to speak with enough clarity that no false comfort keeps either man unprepared.

phrases.translation: and the other will be crucified and the birds will eat from his head.
phrases.explanation: The other will be crucified or hung up and birds will eat from his head transfers the bread image from dream to execution ground. Crucifixion in the ancient setting need not carry every later Roman association, yet public exposure after death is part of the horror. Joseph gives the painful side without theatrical cruelty. A truthful interpreter cannot sell hope to both customers when the signs point in opposite directions.

phrases.translation: The matter about which you inquired has been decided.”
phrases.explanation: The matter is decreed closes negotiation over the interpretation as if the seal has already been placed. This certainty separates revelation given knowledge from a guess offered for approval. It also gives the condemned man whatever little time remains for repentance after hearing the foundation of faith first. The sermon before interpretation now looks pastoral rather than delayed, because one listener was standing at the edge of his life.

phrases.translation: Then he said to the one he knew would survive, “Mention me in the presence of your master.”
phrases.explanation: Mention me before your lord asks the surviving cupbearer to use restored access for an innocent prisoner. Joseph takes a lawful human means without surrendering his theology of divine judgment. Human recommendation is not presented as betrayal of trust in God, since the whole story works through caravans, households, wardens, and courts. The sentence however prepares one of the most painful small failures in the narrative.

phrases.translation: But Satan made him forget to mention Joseph to his master, so he remained in prison for several years
phrases.explanation: Satan made him forget to mention Joseph, or made Joseph forget his Lord in one classical discussion of the pronoun, and the majority reading in the flow assigns forgetfulness to the cupbearer. Several years is expressed with a word often meaning between three and nine. Palace comfort can erase prison gratitude without a dramatic act of malice. Joseph greatest earthly contact simply resumes pouring drinks and leaves the innocent interpreter inside an indefinite administrative sentence.

phrases.translation: And ˹one day˺ the King said, “I dreamt of seven fat cows eaten up by seven skinny ones;
phrases.explanation: Seven fat cows eaten by seven lean cows gives the king a national image in the bodies Egyptians can picture without specialist language. Cattle condition mirrors Nile abundance and scarcity inside an agricultural kingdom. The eating is grotesque because lean years consume stored fat years rather than merely following them. A ruler dreams an economy before his advisers can reduce it to court entertainment.

phrases.translation: and seven green ears of grain and ˹seven˺ others dry.
phrases.explanation: Seven green ears and others withered repeats the same cycle in grain, allowing season, storage, and bread to join cattle in one policy forecast. Green and dry ears side by side make time visible as texture. The number seven creates a timetable, although no calendar dates are supplied. A dream manageable through preparation has arrived in a palace that needs an interpreter able to connect heaven symbols with granaries.

phrases.translation: O chiefs! Tell me the meaning of my dream if you can interpret dreams.”
phrases.explanation: O council, explain my vision if you interpret dreams exposes the king experts to their own advertised craft. A ruler can command attendance but not knowledge. If you are able leaves room for honesty, a door professional pride often refuses. The story moves from prison competence to palace need, because a whole kingdom crisis will not wait for the court to recover from embarrassment.

phrases.translation: They replied, “These are confused visions and we do not know the interpretation of such dreams.”
phrases.explanation: Confused dreams and we know no interpretation gives the council a vocabulary for dismissing the symbol while admitting limitation. Their answer can sound honest, yet calling the royal vision a jumble also protects them from examining an uncomfortable warning. Courts may prefer to declare a problem incoherent when nobody present can solve it. The verse leaves a silence at the centre of power large enough for a forgotten cupbearer to enter.

phrases.translation: ˹Finally,˺ the surviving ex-prisoner remembered ˹Joseph˺ after a long time and said, “I will tell you its interpretation, so send me forth ˹to Joseph˺.”
phrases.explanation: The saved man remembers after a long time, an ordinary memory event with national consequences. Palace routine had covered Joseph name until a similar problem knocked on the same mental door. I will inform you and send me turns belated gratitude into action without a confession scene about the forgotten years. Providence uses even an imperfect friend, although the delay remains morally visible to every reader who has waited for help.

phrases.translation: ˹He said,˺ “Joseph, O man of truth! Interpret for us ˹the dream of˺ seven fat cows eaten up by seven skinny ones;
phrases.explanation: Joseph, O man of truth addresses the prisoner by the quality that will soon decide a legal case as well as a dream. The cupbearer knows from experience that his interpretations arrive exactly as spoken. Seven fat cows eaten by lean ones is repeated without ornament because accuracy matters in transmitting a royal report. A name earned in a cell begins travelling back toward the throne room through another person mouth.

phrases.translation: and seven green ears of grain and ˹seven˺ others dry, so that I may return to the people and let them know.”
phrases.explanation: Seven green and withered ears complete the question, while so I may return to the people and they may know gives knowledge a public purpose. Interpretation here is not a private trick to free Joseph alone. It must travel upward into policy and downward into farms, storehouses, markets, and households. The messenger wants to carry more than a riddle answer. He carries years of preparation compressed into a pattern an entire country can act on.

phrases.translation: Joseph replied, “You will plant ˹grain˺ for seven consecutive years, leaving in the ear whatever you will harvest,
phrases.explanation: You will sow seven years diligently turns survival into labour before scarcity arrives. Leaving harvested grain in its ear except a little eaten is storage technology in early explanation, preserving kernels from rot and pests better in husk. Joseph does not counsel passive awe at a prophecy. He gives an agricultural protocol, because knowing the future under God should increase responsibility rather than replace work with religious excitement.

phrases.translation: except for the little you will eat
phrases.explanation: Except a little you eat limits consumption during abundance without demanding starvation in the fat years. A disciplined nation must eat, celebrate, and still remember a date its children cannot yet see. Little is measured against the harvest, so surplus becomes a public trust. The ethics of plenty sits inside these few words, since granaries are filled by many small decisions not to consume tomorrow at today table.

phrases.translation: Then after that will come seven years of great hardship which will consume whatever you have saved,
phrases.explanation: Seven severe years will consume what was stored, making the lean cows of the dream operate through ration lines and dwindling reserves. Consumption gives famine agency because a whole society eats its way through memory stored in grain. Preparation changes the scene from panic to managed hardship. The interpretation now includes a warning that reserves are not magic. They must be guarded against corruption and released with enough order to last the full period.

phrases.translation: except the little you will store ˹for seed˺
phrases.explanation: Except a little you preserve or keep for sowing protects the seed needed after famine ends. Eating the last seed in the final hungry month would turn survival into agricultural death. Joseph planning reaches beyond emergency relief into recovery, a feature rulers often neglect while seeking applause. Wisdom is shown by what is withheld from even righteous distribution, because next year field is also a hungry neighbour in embryo.

phrases.translation: Then after that will come a year in which people will receive abundant rain and they will press ˹oil and wine˺.”
phrases.explanation: A year in which people are rained on and press grapes or olives adds hope beyond the dream named fourteen years. Joseph tells more than the question strictly asked, giving the nation a horizon after rationing. Pressing signals orchards, vineyards, oil, and ordinary celebration returning to hands that had measured famine portions. Ending the interpretation with rain keeps endurance from becoming despair, because people can preserve seed more bravely when they can picture a green year beyond.

phrases.translation: The King ˹then˺ said, “Bring him to me.” When the messenger came to him,
phrases.explanation: Bring him to me carries Joseph from prison competence into royal curiosity at last. The messenger arrival could have become a rushed exit after years of unjust confinement. Instead the story slows down at the threshold because reputation remains unresolved. A prisoner useful to the state might be released as a favoured technician while the original lie survives. Joseph wants the record opened before the new title covers it.

phrases.translation: Joseph said, “Go back to your master and ask him about the case of the women who cut their hands.
phrases.explanation: Return to your lord and ask about the women who cut their hands avoids naming the minister wife directly while identifying the case unmistakably. He asks for inquiry rather than revenge. Their hands function as the public exhibit through which the king can investigate a banquet many elite witnesses attended. The restraint is remarkable because freedom is visible in the corridor, yet Joseph chooses vindication over a quick change of clothes.

phrases.translation: Surely my Lord has ˹full˺ knowledge of their cunning.”
phrases.explanation: My Lord knows their scheme places the investigation under a knowledge already complete. Joseph does not plead as though the king verdict creates innocence. He asks the court to catch up with what heaven knows. Scheme returns from his prison prayer, now to be examined by the same ruling order that benefited from silence. The sentence turns a release order into a reopening of evidence.

phrases.translation: The King asked ˹the women˺, “What did you get when you tried to seduce Joseph?”
phrases.explanation: The king asks what was your affair when you sought to seduce Joseph, shifting the inquiry from private household management to sovereign investigation. His phrasing assumes their collective role without yet naming verdicts. Women who once gossiped in drawing rooms now stand before a ruler because the forgotten prisoner gift has become nationally valuable. Power can reopen a case for self interested reasons while God uses the hearing for fuller justice.

phrases.translation: They replied, “Allah forbid! We know nothing indecent about him.”
phrases.explanation: God forbid, we know no evil about him gives Joseph a public character certificate from the very circle recruited against him. Their sentence does not yet confess every detail of pressure, but it clears the accused in the only respect he requested. Hands cut at a banquet now produce verbal testimony. Elite society is required to say aloud what the torn shirt already proved in a corridor years earlier.

phrases.translation: Then the Chief Minister’s wife admitted, “Now the truth has come to light.
phrases.explanation: Now the truth has become clear is spoken by the minister wife as concealment collapses in the royal hearing. Her sentence has the force of a public unveiling after years in which an innocent man carried the practical punishment. Truth appearing does not rewind prison time, yet it changes how every later honour will be understood. A confession delayed can still cleanse the record even while exposing the cost of delay.

phrases.translation: It was I who tried to seduce him, and he is surely truthful
phrases.explanation: I sought to seduce him and he is among the truthful completes the reversal in the principal voice. The person who once asked what penalty a supposed offender deserved now names herself as pursuer and him as truthful. Joseph earlier title from the cupbearer receives legal confirmation. A story about shirts and speech reaches its cleanest sentence when the person with most status to lose tells the simple fact all the evidence had been carrying.

phrases.translation: From this, Joseph should know that I did not speak dishonestly about him in his absence,
phrases.explanation: That is so he may know I did not betray him in absence is commonly read as Joseph later explanation of why he requested inquiry, although narrative voice at this point has invited interpretive discussion. If Joseph speaks, he wants the master to know prison did not conceal a secret violation of trust. Vindication is aimed at moral fact rather than public applause because loyalty in absence is exactly what could not be photographed by a tear.

phrases.translation: for Allah certainly does not guide the scheming of the dishonest
phrases.explanation: Allah does not guide the plot of betrayers gives the confession a universal law. Schemes built on false accusation may occupy years, prisons, and drawing rooms, yet they are not given final direction by God. The sentence comforts people whose vindication is still in transit. A lie can be institutionally successful while remaining cosmically lost, because its end is scheduled by a Lord who never mistakes a prisoner record for the truth.

phrases.translation: And I do not seek to free myself from blame, for indeed the soul is ever inclined to evil,
phrases.explanation: I do not acquit myself begins a confession that early readers assigned most often to the minister wife continuing after truth emerges, with some discussion in the tradition around speaker changes. No self acquittal means she refuses a final cosmetic sentence about irresistible beauty. The soul commanding evil explains persistence without turning desire into an external excuse. Personal responsibility finally enters the room where blame shifting once ruled the furniture.

phrases.translation: except those shown mercy by my Lord.
phrases.explanation: Except what my Lord has mercy on places escape from the commanding soul under mercy rather than willpower mythology. Joseph purity and the woman confession now meet at the same divine gate, although their histories differ. Mercy can restrain a soul before sin or awaken it after sin. The phrase keeps moral psychology humble because no character in the story becomes safe merely by knowing the right vocabulary.

phrases.translation: Surely my Lord is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”
phrases.explanation: My Lord is Forgiving and Merciful ends confession on the names needed by a guilty speaker and a wronged listener alike. Forgiveness gives the woman a future not frozen at the banquet threat if her repentance is sincere. Mercy also explains why Joseph story continues without his demanding her destruction. The hearing cleans the record and then leaves souls with God, a pattern that will govern the brothers return at the end.

phrases.translation: The King said, “Bring him to me. I will employ him exclusively in my service.”
phrases.explanation: Bring him so I may attach him especially to myself upgrades Joseph from useful prisoner to close royal servant before a job description is negotiated. Special attachment promises access, trust, and status at court. The king has seen interpretation and vindication but not yet administration. His instinct is to secure the man whose knowledge might preserve the kingdom, a recognition that the state most needs the person it allowed to disappear.

phrases.translation: And when Joseph spoke to him, the King said, “Today you are highly esteemed and fully trusted by us.”
phrases.explanation: When he speaks with him the king declares him established and trusted, adding character judgment to the dream result. Established can mean secure in position, while trusted reflects the now public innocence and Joseph language. Today marks the social date when the cell record is no longer allowed to define him at court. One conversation cannot create such trust from nothing. It confirms a reputation formed through prison, cupbearer testimony, and the women hearing.

phrases.translation: Joseph proposed, “Put me in charge of the store-houses of the land, for I am truly reliable and adept.”
phrases.explanation: Set me over the storehouses of the earth is Joseph request for the specific office his interpretation requires. He does not ask for a palace ornament or revenge against the minister household. Knowing and guarding in the translation sense of knowledgeable and trustworthy names the two qualifications famine policy needs. Competence without trust would invite theft, and trust without competence would waste grain. The verse permits a qualified believer to name his fitness for public service without false modesty.

phrases.translation: This is how We established Joseph in the land to settle wherever he pleased.
phrases.explanation: Thus We established Joseph in the land to settle where he will completes the phrase first used when he entered the Egyptian house as a slave. Establishment has ripened from placement into authority across years the reader can now reread as preparation. Land that received him in merchandise chains becomes the territory his decisions can organise. The verse does not pretend the pit was pleasant. It shows the destination hidden inside routes nobody would choose.

phrases.translation: We shower Our mercy on whoever We will, and We never discount the reward of the good-doers
phrases.explanation: We strike with Our mercy whom We will in the sense of bestowing it, and never waste the reward of good doers turns promotion into theology. Joseph office is mercy before it is salary, while his excellence under betrayal, seduction, and imprisonment remains part of the account. Reward not wasted speaks to every forgotten prisoner season in which goodness seemed unrecorded. The public palace result is one instalment, not the sole proof that heaven was watching.

phrases.translation: And the reward of the Hereafter is far better for those who are faithful and are mindful ˹of Allah˺
phrases.explanation: The reward of the Hereafter is better for believers who are mindful prevents governmental success from becoming the story highest prize. Joseph might reach the end of a human ambition arc here, yet the narration lifts the ceiling again. Faith and God consciousness through humiliation and power earn more than office can contain. Readers who never receive a palace are assured that the palace itself is not the greatest form of divine payment.

phrases.translation: And Joseph’s brothers came and entered his presence. He recognized them but they were unaware of who he really was
phrases.explanation: Brothers enter Joseph presence for famine grain while he recognises them and they remain unaware, fulfilling the pit promise from an angle nobody in the room understands. Time, language, clothing, office, and Egyptian presentation have changed the child they abandoned. Recognition gives Joseph complete power over the pace of truth. The scene becomes a test of what a wronged man does when revenge is administratively easy and mercy requires design.

phrases.translation: When he had provided them with their supplies, he demanded, “Bring me your brother on your father’s side.
phrases.explanation: After supplying their loads Joseph demands the brother from their father, meaning Benjamin, as proof of their account and a condition for future trade. The demand is staged as state policy rather than family longing so no recognition leaks too soon. Joseph needs Benjamin brought safely into a plan that will also test whether brothers protect a favoured younger son differently now. Food becomes the rope drawing a separated household together.

phrases.translation: Do you not see that I give full measure and I am the best of hosts
phrases.explanation: Do you not see I give full measure and am the best of hosts uses his present generosity as evidence of good faith. Full measure stands in pointed contrast to merchants who diminish scales, and to brothers who once gave Joseph a false measure of protection. Hospitality disarms suspicion because a starving delegation has just been treated well. He builds trust with grain while quietly preparing a moral courtroom inside a relief office.

phrases.translation: But if you do not bring him to me ˹next time˺,
phrases.explanation: If you do not bring him there is no measure for you converts Benjamin absence into a supply crisis for the whole family. This pressure is strong medicine, yet in famine administration identity checks and household counts determine rations. Joseph applies the condition to force a second journey under his design. The brothers cannot simply bury another younger brother in a story because the Egyptian office will compare faces and numbers.

phrases.translation: I will have no grain for you, nor will you ever come close to me again.”
phrases.explanation: Nor come near me closes access to the minister himself, making distance from the source of grain part of the penalty. A family once pushed Joseph far away to gain their father face. Now an unrecognised Joseph threatens to push them away unless the other favoured son is brought near. The reversal is exact without being crude revenge, because the aim is reunion and testing rather than starvation of his father house.

phrases.translation: They promised, “We will try to convince his father to let him come. We will certainly do ˹our best˺.”
phrases.explanation: We will solicit him from his father and indeed we will do it uses a verb of gradual coaxing in early explanation. The brothers already know Jacob trust has been spent and must be earned back through persuasion. Their confidence sounds practical, yet the reader hears an old sentence forming again around a younger brother. The question carried home is whether hunger and a solemn setting can make different men of repeat actors.

phrases.translation: Joseph ordered his servants to put his brothers’ money back into their saddlebags so that they would find it when they returned to their family and perhaps they would come back
phrases.explanation: Put their merchandise or payment into their saddlebags so they may recognise it and return adds a silent gift inside the rationing plan. Returning the price can relieve a poor family, prove Egyptian goodwill, and give them means for the next purchase. Joseph generosity is strategically hidden because open charity from a minister might raise questions. His brothers will discover that the office which threatened exclusion also financed their return, complicating the story they tell Jacob.

phrases.translation: When Joseph’s brothers returned to their father, they pleaded, “O our father!
phrases.explanation: Returned to their father, they begin with measure has been denied rather than with news of generous treatment. Crisis language is effective at a hungry household table. The brothers frame Benjamin as the key needed to unlock food rather than as a child entrusted to their damaged record. Jacob hears a policy argument shaped by need, and the old outing request begins repeating itself with an Egyptian seal on the paper.

phrases.translation: We have been denied ˹further˺ supplies. So send our brother with us so that we may receive our measure,
phrases.explanation: Send our brother with us that we may measure repeats the vocabulary of collecting their share under a ration system. Benjamin presence will add legitimacy and perhaps an additional load. The economic case is honest enough, which makes it difficult for Jacob to dismiss as mere manipulation. The story becomes morally interesting because truth, need, and Joseph hidden design now pull in the same direction while memory pulls the father back.

phrases.translation: and we will definitely watch over him.”
phrases.explanation: We will guard him is the exact promise previously broken around Joseph, now spoken under the shadow of that failure. A repeated sentence can either expose unchanged character or mark the beginning of repair. This time cattle, provisions, hunger, and an Egyptian registry create external checks. The verse deliberately makes the reader hear the old script so later conduct at the cup incident will prove whether words have acquired new substance.

phrases.translation: He responded, “Should I trust you with him as I once trusted you with his brother ˹Joseph˺?
phrases.explanation: Shall I trust you with him except as I trusted you with his brother refuses polite amnesia at the family table. Jacob names the failed custody without rehearsing the wolf lie again. His question asks the sons to sit inside the consequence of their history rather than market a fresh guarantee as if no past existed. Trust, once spent on a child life, cannot be renewed with the same sentence alone.

phrases.translation: But ˹only˺ Allah is the best Protector, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful.”
phrases.explanation: Allah is the best guardian and most merciful of the merciful gives Jacob a place to stand between suspicion and family starvation. He neither calls his sons reliable nor treats hunger as a fictional pressure. Ultimate custody is transferred to God while a practical decision remains unfinished. Beautiful patience has matured into theological risk management, where a father can acknowledge damaged trust and still act for the survival of the whole house.

phrases.translation: When they opened their bags, they discovered that their money had been returned to them.
phrases.explanation: Opening the baggage and finding their payment returned changes the emotional weather of negotiation. What reads as an accounting mistake to them is a planted sign from Joseph, although nobody in Canaan can decode it yet. Goodwill discovered inside grain bags makes the Egyptian minister look less like a trap. The event also tests the brothers honesty, since unspent payment could quietly disappear before their father sees it.

phrases.translation: They argued, “O our father! What more can we ask for?
phrases.explanation: O our father, what more do we seek turns returned merchandise into a rhetorical flourish. They have grain for the present and capital for another trip, a combination hunger makes difficult to refuse. Yet notice how quickly money strengthens an argument about entrusting Benjamin. Jacob still has to separate an encouraging sign from a guarantee about his sons conduct. Evidence about the minister generosity does not by itself repair the old wolf account.

phrases.translation: Here is our money, fully returned to us. Now we can buy more food for our family.
phrases.explanation: This payment of ours is returned lets the coins speak in front of the father as the shirt once spoke falsely. Physical evidence has entered the family debate again, only now it genuinely helps. We will provision our family repeats their role as suppliers during famine. The brothers stand to gain food and standing by success. Their willingness to display the returned goods is one small honest movement in a long repair.

phrases.translation: We will watch over our brother, and obtain an extra camel-load of grain. That load can be easily secured.”
phrases.explanation: We will guard our brother and gain a camel load joins the old promise with a measurable benefit. An extra load sounds easy in their mouth, almost a salesman closing line under famine distress. Jacob must weigh a starving household against a sentence that once ended in a bloody shirt. The dramatic pressure lies in that balance, because refusing also has a human cost and is not automatically the righteous answer.

phrases.translation: Jacob insisted, “I will not send him with you until you give me a solemn oath by Allah that you will certainly bring him back to me, unless you are totally overpowered.”
phrases.explanation: I will not send him until you give me a covenant from Allah raises the promise from family assurance to an oath before God. Bring him back unless you are surrounded or overpowered writes a force majeure exception into the agreement. Jacob is not being merely theatrical. He creates the strongest accountability available inside a household where ordinary promises have collapsed. Hunger may move the decision, but language will remember the terms.

phrases.translation: Then after they had given him their oaths, he concluded, “Allah is a Witness to what we have said.”
phrases.explanation: When they give their covenant he says Allah is trustee over what we say, appointing a witness no caravan distance can evade. Trustee language echoes Joseph earlier theology of God as guardian over matters people cannot control. The father cannot ride with every mile of road. He places the conversation itself under custody, so each son carries a spoken document that will judge him when Benjamin is seized.

phrases.translation: He then instructed ˹them˺, “O my sons! Do not enter ˹the city˺ all through one gate, but through separate gates.
phrases.explanation: Do not enter by one gate but by separate gates gives practical protection against envy, suspicion, or the evil eye in the explanations offered by many commentators. Eleven strong foreign brothers entering together could attract attention in a rationed capital. Jacob remains a careful father even after surrendering custody to God. Taking means and trusting God are not rivals in this household when each is given its proper rank.

phrases.translation: I cannot help you against ˹what is destined by˺ Allah in the least.
phrases.explanation: I cannot avail you against Allah at all limits fatherly strategy before it can become superstition. Gates can reduce a visible risk without editing destiny. Decision belongs only to Allah repeats the prison sermon of Joseph in his father mouth, joining separated generations by theology. Jacob is teaching the sons a hierarchy of causation as they leave, perhaps the lesson their treatment of Joseph most needed decades earlier.

phrases.translation: It is only Allah Who decides. In Him I put my trust.
phrases.explanation: In Him I trust makes trust a deliberate act after planning has done its modest work. It is not a slogan spread over passivity since gates, oaths, food calculations, and family arguments all remain in the scene. Jacob lets Benjamin travel while inwardly transferring the final result. The reader sees beautiful patience become action rather than a frozen pose by an empty chair.

phrases.translation: And in Him let the faithful put their trust.”
phrases.explanation: Let those who trust put trust in Him widens Jacob sentence beyond this caravan into a rule for every frightened guardian. People can lock doors, divide entrances, write covenants, and still meet a future no device secures. Trust gathers those devices after use and prevents them from becoming idols. The verse speaks directly to the chapter recurring question of who truly protects a beloved child on a road controlled by others.

phrases.translation: Then when they entered as their father had instructed them, this did not help them against ˹the Will of˺ Allah whatsoever.
phrases.explanation: Entering as instructed does not avail against Allah is narrated before any benefit can be exaggerated. Obedience to Jacob has personal and social value even if it cannot alter the coming cup incident. The verse separates a wise measure from an absolute shield with unusual clarity. It protects readers from turning prophetic advice into magical technique, as if heavenly results could be purchased through a gate pattern.

phrases.translation: It was just a desire in Jacob’s heart which he satisfied.
phrases.explanation: It was a need in Jacob soul that he fulfilled gives affection and anxiety a dignified place inside obedience. A father may need to act on care allowed to him even while knowing God decision stands above it. The phrase has been read as his wish to protect them from the eye or public suspicion. Either way, emotion is neither mocked nor mistaken for control. Responsible tenderness can be meaningful without being omnipotent.

phrases.translation: He was truly blessed with ˹great˺ knowledge because of what We had taught him, but most people have no knowledge
phrases.explanation: He possessed knowledge because We taught him while most people do not know returns Jacob discernment to divine teaching. The knowledge shown is practical and theological at once, because he uses gates while denying their independence. Many people choose either reliance without means or means without reliance. Jacob holds both in proper order, which is why the verse pauses over a travel instruction that could look minor beside famine and kings.

phrases.translation: When they entered Joseph’s presence, he called his brother ˹Benjamin˺ aside, and confided ˹to him˺, “I am indeed your brother ˹Joseph˺!
phrases.explanation: Joseph takes his brother to himself and says I am your brother gives Benjamin the first private door into a truth the others cannot yet hear.
