Full brotherhood through their mother makes this recognition especially intimate after decades of silence. Joseph chooses a controlled disclosure that will help Benjamin endure the coming accusation without panic. A secret used to protect reconciliation now replaces the brothers old secret used to destroy a child.

phrases.translation: So do not feel distressed about what they have been doing.”
phrases.explanation: Do not grieve over what they used to do tells Benjamin how to carry the next stage and perhaps how to read the family past. He may have grown up in the weather created by Joseph absence without knowing its cause. Joseph does not recruit him into hatred at the moment of reunion. The first gift between brothers is calm inside a plan that will look, for a few public minutes, like disgrace and theft.

phrases.translation: When Joseph had provided them with supplies, he slipped the royal cup into his brother’s bag.
phrases.explanation: Placing the drinking cup in Benjamin saddlebag creates a controlled legal test around another favoured son in the brothers custody. The cup is a royal measuring vessel in several explanations, linking value, state authority, and grain distribution. Joseph design will force the older brothers to choose between abandoning Benjamin to Egypt and standing in the breach. A planted object becomes x ray equipment for a conscience under pressure.

phrases.translation: Then a herald cried, “O people of the caravan! You must be thieves!”
phrases.explanation: A caller cries that the caravan are thieves turns a family test into a public roadside accusation. The brothers must stop while still close enough to be searched and shamed before strangers. Their earlier crime was secret and their lie domestic. Now suspicion arrives with witnesses, procedures, and an object that will be found exactly where Joseph placed it. The story gives them a second younger brother crisis under lights they cannot dim.

phrases.translation: They asked, turning back, “What have you lost?”
phrases.explanation: What are you missing shows the brothers turning back with enough composure to ask for details, unaware that the answer sits inside Benjamin bag. Their question buys a little procedural dignity after being publicly named thieves. It also begins a dialogue in which each side will state a rule before evidence appears. Joseph plan depends on agreed words spoken before the search, because the test is as legal as it is emotional.

phrases.translation: The herald ˹along with the guards˺ replied, “We have lost the King’s measuring cup.
phrases.explanation: The king drinking cup or measuring vessel is named, connecting palace service with the ration system through which the brothers just passed. A royal object carries state honour, so theft would be more than private property loss. In the context of famine, a measuring cup also symbolises the exact distribution Joseph claimed as his policy. The object supposedly stolen is an instrument of justice in the food lines.

phrases.translation: And whoever brings it will be awarded a camel-load ˹of grain˺. I guarantee it.”
phrases.explanation: Whoever brings it gets a camel load and I guarantee it adds reward and official surety to the search announcement. A camel load is a meaningful prize in famine and mirrors the extra load promised through Benjamin presence. Public procedure creates a stage where the caravan can cooperate before force is needed. The herald confidence also tightens the net, because an announced reward tells every camel driver that the missing object matters.

phrases.translation: Joseph’s brothers replied, “By Allah! You know well that we did not come to cause trouble in the land, nor are we thieves.”
phrases.explanation: By Allah, you know we did not come to spread corruption nor were we thieves gives the brothers a sincere oath this time. They truly have not stolen the cup, although their public innocence in the present case stands beside a hidden older crime. The story allows guilty people to tell the truth about a later event. Their trouble is more complex than a simple label, and God court can distinguish charges they deserve from one they do not.

phrases.translation: Joseph’s men asked, “What should be the price for theft, if you are lying?”
phrases.explanation: What is the penalty if you are liars asks the accused to specify the law before the object is produced. This is the hinge of Joseph design, because Egyptian law apparently would not let him detain Benjamin in the desired way. The question gives the brothers agency in the courtroom being built around them. Their own family or religious rule will supply the sentence, teaching that words spoken in confidence can become the frame of a trial.

phrases.translation: Joseph’s brothers responded, “The price will be ˹the enslavement of˺ the one in whose bag the cup is found.
phrases.explanation: The one in whose bag it is found himself becomes the penalty expresses a rule in which the thief is handed over or enslaved to the wronged party. Early commentators linked this to Jacob law or custom as distinct from Egyptian punishment. The brothers pronounce it while certain of innocence, unknowingly authorising Benjamin detention. A legal sentence they choose will now force the question of whether they abandon another favoured son to permanent service.

phrases.translation: That is how we punish the wrongdoers.”
phrases.explanation: Thus we repay wrongdoers completes their confident statement with a community standard they claim to uphold. Wrongdoer language has followed Joseph since the seduction room, where he refused to join them. At the roadside it becomes a technical category based on evidence. The brothers cannot easily call the rule barbaric after producing it themselves, so their later plea must ask for personal substitution rather than dispute the procedure.

phrases.translation: Joseph began searching their bags before that of his brother ˹Benjamin˺, then brought it out of Benjamin’s bag.
phrases.explanation: Searching their bags before Benjamin bag builds fairness into the performance and prolongs the brothers hope one sack at a time. Beginning with him would expose the design and invite protest. When the cup emerges from the youngest load, public procedure has already established sequence, witnesses, penalty, and the accused admission of the system. The object itself now performs the role shirts played twice before in deciding a contested story.

phrases.translation: This is how We inspired Joseph to plan. He could not have taken his brother under the King’s law, but Allah had so willed.
phrases.explanation: Thus We planned for Joseph identifies divine planning behind the legal route, because under the king law he could not simply seize his brother as the family penalty allowed. Plan in this language answers human schemes without endorsing every deceptive method in ordinary imitation. The goal is custody for reunion and moral testing, not enrichment. God knowledge finds a path between Egyptian statute, family law, famine politics, and a father oath.

phrases.translation: We elevate in rank whoever We will. But above those ranking in knowledge is the One All-Knowing
phrases.explanation: We raise degrees whom We will and above every knower is the All Knowing places Joseph cleverness under a higher knowledge. His ranking has grown through dream, prison, interpretation, administration, and now legal design, yet he remains a servant taught by God. The sentence prevents a reader from worshipping strategic brilliance. Each expert in the story meets a limit, while divine knowledge keeps every plan inside a wider and kinder architecture.

phrases.translation: ˹To distance themselves,˺ Joseph’s brothers argued, “If he has stolen, so did his ˹full˺ brother before.”
phrases.explanation: If he steals, a brother of his stole before distances the older sons from Benjamin by smearing Joseph childhood in a report they may have inherited or invented. The sentence is a small relapse at the exact moment unity is needed. It suggests that full brothers carry a family defect while half brothers from another side remain respectable. Old envy can survive inside men who are otherwise beginning to repair a greater crime.

phrases.translation: But Joseph suppressed his outrage—revealing nothing to them—and said ˹to himself˺,
phrases.explanation: Joseph hides his anger or hurt and does not reveal it to them, an administrative silence with decades of personal history inside it. Another false story about him is spoken to his face by the same family that fabricated wolf evidence. Restraint protects the larger design from collapsing into an argument over a childhood anecdote. Power is shown not by using the throne to answer every insult immediately but by knowing which truth must wait.

phrases.translation: “You are in such an evil position, and Allah knows best ˹the truth of˺ what you claim.”
phrases.explanation: You are worse in position and Allah knows best what you describe is spoken in his heart according to the common reading. Their position is worse because accusers with a drowned secret of selling a brother are lecturing on inherited theft. Joseph leaves the inner sentence with God rather than making courtroom satisfaction his aim. The verse lets readers see pain under the minister mask while respect grows for a ruler who can postpone vindication.

phrases.translation: They appealed, “O Chief Minister! He has a very old father, so take one of us instead.
phrases.explanation: He has an aged father, take one of us instead of him marks the great reversal in the brothers moral story. The same company that removed one favoured son for access to their father now offers their own bodies to spare another favoured son for that father sake. Age and grief enter the plea because Benjamin legal status cannot be separated from the old man waiting in Canaan. Their oath has begun changing conduct under pressure.

phrases.translation: We surely see you as one of the good-doers.”
phrases.explanation: We see you among the good doers addresses Joseph public generosity with full measure and returned payment, although they still do not know his name. The phrase repeats the prisoners description of him, connecting cell and court through reputation. They ask excellence to bend a rule they themselves proposed. Their appeal is not legally strong, yet it is humanly revealing because the easy road home without Benjamin no longer feels available to them.

phrases.translation: Joseph responded, “Allah forbid that we should take other than the one with whom we found our property. Otherwise, we would surely be unjust.”
phrases.explanation: God forbid we take except the one with whom our property was found refuses substitution as injustice, even when offered by volunteers. A younger brother cannot be exchanged like a sack weight between adults. Joseph uses rigorous fairness to raise the cost of the test to its climax. Would they leave now that mercy by substitution is forbidden. The title wrongdoers comes back as a line he will not cross although his whole design is hidden from them.

phrases.translation: When they lost all hope in him, they spoke privately.
phrases.explanation: When they despair of him they withdraw in private counsel, echoing the first conspiratorial meeting while reversing its purpose. Private speech can design a crime or design accountability depending on what the participants now fear. They no longer ask how to face their father with a persuasive prop. They ask how covenant and failure constrain their bodies. The room tone has changed because the oldest voice can name the past directly.

phrases.translation: The eldest of them said, “Do you not know that your father had taken a solemn oath by Allah from you,
phrases.explanation: Do you not know your father took a covenant from Allah from you makes the oath an active resident in the conversation. Jacob is absent geographically while his spoken terms govern the Egyptian road. The eldest does not allow necessity or Benjamin apparent theft to erase their signature. A covenant works precisely when circumstances become complicated enough to tempt people into calling old promises impractical.

phrases.translation: nor how you failed him regarding Joseph before?
phrases.explanation: And your earlier neglect concerning Joseph finally names the buried crime inside the group without an audience to impress. This is a hinge of the whole book because repair cannot grow stronger than truth in private. The same brothers once agreed on a false blood story. Now their internal history lesson includes their own dereliction. No flowers of apology yet reach Joseph, but denial has begun losing territory in the only room where it fully ruled.

phrases.translation: So I am not leaving this land until my father allows me to, or Allah decides for me.
phrases.explanation: I will not leave the land until my father permits me or Allah judges for me turns the eldest body into collateral for the oath. Staying in Egypt costs him homecoming and reputation while giving Jacob evidence that this is not another casual loss. Earlier the sons returned together with a polished lie. Now one refuses the comfort of the group itinerary because returning empty would make him participate in a second abandonment.

phrases.translation: For He is the Best of Judges
phrases.explanation: He is the best of judges resolves the eldest dilemma without pretending he controls Benjamin release. Human courts under Joseph have reached a limit, and Jacob permission may take a journey to request. Divine judgment can mean an opening in Egypt or acceptance of consequence under God. The phrase creates patience with unfinished business, a new skill in brothers who once solved family tension through one afternoon at a well.

phrases.translation: Return to your father and say, ‘O our father! Your son committed theft.
phrases.explanation: Return and say your son has stolen scripts the report to Jacob with unwanted precision. Unlike the wolf story, this sentence describes the Egyptian legal finding as they understand it. They cannot honestly pronounce Benjamin inner action with certainty, yet the cup in his sack is public fact. The eldest instructions already show a mind sorting what was seen from what can be moralised, a discipline absent when false blood was enough.

phrases.translation: We testify only to what we know. We could not guard against the unforeseen
phrases.explanation: We testify only to what we know and were not guardians of the unseen gives the report an epistemic boundary worthy of the shirt trial. They cannot know whether Benjamin planned theft, whether someone planted the cup, or how an oath should cover invisible events. Their task is to name observed facts and admit the limit. This is a huge change from manufacturing certainty around a wolf attack none of them saw.

phrases.translation: Ask ˹the people of˺ the land where we were and the caravan we travelled with. We are certainly telling the truth.’”
phrases.explanation: Ask the town and caravan invites Jacob to verify the story through witnesses outside the family interest. A town full of officials and a caravan of travellers can confirm the search sequence if not Joseph hidden design. We are truthful now attaches itself to checkable evidence rather than theatrical tears. The brothers have learned that trust destroyed by a crafted shirt must be approached with outside references, even when the conclusion still hurts.

phrases.translation: He cried, “No! Your souls must have tempted you to do something ˹evil˺.
phrases.explanation: Jacob responds that their souls have made a matter easy again, repeating the diagnosis from the night of false blood. He may not know the real design, yet his history with their reporting makes a simple theft verdict suspect. Repetition lets readers hear how a father files a second catastrophe beside the first unsolved loss. Suspicion alone is not knowledge, so Jacob pain remains in a fog where neither son can be reached.

phrases.translation: So ˹I am left with nothing but˺ beautiful patience! I trust Allah will return them all to me.
phrases.explanation: Beautiful patience rises again, only now hope has a wider sentence attached to it. Perhaps Allah will bring them all to me includes Joseph, Benjamin, and perhaps the son remaining in Egypt within one imagined return. Patience has not become cold resignation over the decades. It holds an address for future reunion while accepting that current evidence cannot produce the road. Waiting is transformed into expectancy governed by God knowledge.

phrases.translation: Surely He ˹alone˺ is the All-Knowing, All-Wise.”
phrases.explanation: He is the All Knowing and All Wise gives Jacob a place to set two missing sons, one detained son, a suspected theft, and a caravan story he cannot verify in person. Knowledge covers facts while wisdom covers why reunion is delayed so painfully. His faith does not supply a detective report. It supplies confidence that the incomplete file is complete somewhere safe, which allows him to grieve without pronouncing the story finished.

phrases.translation: He turned away from them, lamenting, “Alas, poor Joseph!” And his eyes turned white out of the grief he suppressed
phrases.explanation: Turning from them and crying alas for Joseph shows that Benjamin loss has reopened the oldest wound rather than replacing it. Grief can store a name for decades and speak it in the first person when a second absence strikes. His eyes whitened from sorrow, commonly understood as blindness or severe dimming through prolonged weeping. Beautiful patience and physical devastation coexist, disproving any idea that patient faith makes a parent unable to feel catastrophe.

phrases.translation: They said, “By Allah! You will not cease to remember Joseph until you lose your health or ˹even˺ your life.”
phrases.explanation: By Allah you will not stop remembering Joseph until you waste away or die is the sons attempt to manage a grief that accuses them daily. Their concern may contain real fear for his health alongside exhaustion at the living memorial. A person can become a reminder simply by surviving with a wound others caused and prefer to archive. Jacob remembrance is therefore an ethical presence in the house, not only a symptom their advice can cure.

phrases.translation: He replied, “I complain of my anguish and sorrow only to Allah, and I know from Allah what you do not know
phrases.explanation: I complain of my anguish and sorrow only to Allah distinguishes lament directed to God from complaint against God. Jacob spills intensity before the One he trusts rather than demanding his sons become worthy containers for it. I know from Allah what you do not know explains hope without sharing every ground, perhaps knowledge of Joseph dream and divine mercy. Patient sorrow becomes prayerful knowledge, allowing him to sound irrational to the household while standing on a firmer unseen premise.

phrases.translation: O my sons! Go and search ˹diligently˺ for Joseph and his brother.
phrases.explanation: Go and search for Joseph and his brother erupts from grief as action after years in which the older son name could only be an elegy. Jacob commands investigation rather than another caravan report shaped by hunger. Search is a verb of close inquiry, suited to a story where people have repeatedly looked at shirts, bags, cups, and dreams. Even his wording treats Joseph as alive in possibility, refusing the wolf as a sealed file.

phrases.translation: And do not lose hope in the mercy of Allah, for no one loses hope in Allah’s mercy except those with no faith.”
phrases.explanation: Do not despair of Allah relief or spirit gives the quest its theology before passports and provisions are considered. Only disbelieving people despair of that relief because they judge by a closed visible inventory. The sentence is remarkable from a blind father who has just lost a second son. Hope here is not optimism about odds. It is loyalty to a Lord whose capacity is not reduced by a family long experience of absence.

phrases.translation: When they entered Joseph’s presence, they pleaded, “O Chief Minister!
phrases.explanation: When they enter on Joseph again the title minister is spoken by men who have travelled with poverty rather than policy arguments. Their posture has changed from caravan negotiators to petitioners with an ageing blind father and detained brother behind them. Time spent eating famine grain has stripped away the strong company voice heard at the childhood gate. The vocabulary of need is now honest enough to open the recognition scene.

phrases.translation: We and our family have been touched with hardship, and we have brought only a few worthless coins,
phrases.explanation: Hardship has touched us and our family and we brought meagre merchandise lays their whole household condition on the counter. Meagre can mean poor quality goods of little market acceptance, the sort of payment officials might hardly count. The sentence admits they cannot command a full transaction. Those who once sold a brother for counted coins must ask a brother to value their lives beyond the poor goods in their hands.

phrases.translation: but ˹please˺ give us our supplies in full and be charitable to us. Indeed, Allah rewards the charitable.”
phrases.explanation: Give full measure and be charitable to us turns ration language into a request for grace beyond arithmetic. Allah rewards the charitable gives the minister a God centred motive in the same breath. It is an astonishing appeal because they earlier invoked his excellence as a reason to release Benjamin. Now hungry powerlessness completes the lesson. They survive by the full measure of the person they once gave a pit.

phrases.translation: He asked, “Do you remember what you did to Joseph and his brother in your ignorance?”
phrases.explanation: Do you know what you did to Joseph and his brother when you were ignorant finally opens the name. Ignorant diagnoses their past without using the more theatrical label murderers, although murder was debated and abandonment chosen. Joseph asks knowledge rather than reciting their file because he wants conscience awake before identity lands. The pit revelation promised while they do not perceive becomes an adult conversation at the safest moment mercy can control.

phrases.translation: They replied ˹in shock˺, “Are you really Joseph?” He said, “I am Joseph, and here is my brother ˹Benjamin˺!
phrases.explanation: Are you indeed Joseph carries the shock of a voice, face, memory, and question aligning under an Egyptian title. I am Joseph and this is my brother joins the once stolen child with the detained full brother in one living tableau. The two favoured sons stand safely beside each other before the very company built around their separation. Recognition is staged as restoration rather than an ambush.

phrases.translation: Allah has truly been gracious to us. Surely whoever is mindful ˹of Allah˺ and patient,
phrases.explanation: Allah has favoured us assigns the survival of both brothers to God before any accounting begins. Us includes Benjamin, whose detour into detention ended in protection rather than abandonment. Joseph does not begin by saying I have won. He reads private endurance and public office as a shared grace for the family line. That first interpretation of events determines whether confession can happen without fearing a revenge tribunal.

phrases.translation: then certainly Allah never discounts the reward of the good-doers.”
phrases.explanation: Whoever is mindful and patient will not have the reward of good doers wasted gives the story moral in Joseph own mouth. Mindfulness held his conduct in a seduction room while patience held his heart through pit, sale, prison, forgotten years, and tested forgiveness. The brothers hear a universal road instead of a private boast. Excellence hidden in terrible places has been carried intact by a Lord whose accounting never loses a deed.

phrases.translation: They admitted, “By Allah! Allah has truly preferred you over us, and we have surely been sinful.”
phrases.explanation: By Allah, God has preferred you over us and we were sinners unites the confession with the exact comparison that started the crime. They no longer dispute Joseph special place once office, wisdom, chastity, and mercy have displayed it. We were sinners is plain plural responsibility without blaming their father, Satan alone, youth, or one ringleader. After decades of layered stories, ownership takes only one sentence because pride no longer needs a speech to protect it.

phrases.translation: Joseph said, “There is no blame on you today. May Allah forgive you!
phrases.explanation: No reproach on you today is one of the great forgiveness sentences in scripture because today carries all the power required for revenge. Joseph could use grain, law, prison records, and royal authority to settle childhood terror. Instead he cancels blame at the moment after confession and before family logistics begin. Forgiveness comes before proof that they will never fail again, giving mercy the dignity of a gift rather than a payment extracted by perfection.

phrases.translation: He is the Most Merciful of the merciful
phrases.explanation: May Allah forgive you, He is most merciful of the merciful, hands the deeper debt to God after Joseph settles his own claim. A victim can release personal vengeance while recognising that only God can cleanse the soul account. That division protects forgiveness from pretending the crime was small. It also gives brothers a road beyond being tolerated by a powerful sibling, because restored relationship must reach the Lord whose child and prophet they harmed.

phrases.translation: Go with this shirt of mine and cast it over my father’s face, and he will regain his sight.
phrases.explanation: Go with this shirt and cast it on my father face turns cloth into medicine and evidence after shirts carried false blood and a forensic tear. He will become seeing promises physical restoration braided with news that the grief story has ended. The same household object that began as staged proof of death now carries living scent and royal authority. Joseph sends sight home before sending explanations, giving the old father joy in a form his hands can touch.

phrases.translation: Then come back to me with your whole family.”
phrases.explanation: Bring all your family to me turns reconciliation into migration, because famine and reunion share the same road. Joseph does not ask Jacob to symbolically forgive a distant minister by letter. He gathers parents, brothers, households, and children under Egyptian provision. The child cast into a land now casts open that land to the entire family. Providence has been building both a personal apology room and a national settlement through one grain administration.

phrases.translation: When the caravan departed ˹from Egypt˺, their father said ˹to those around him˺,
phrases.explanation: When the caravan departed, their father detects Joseph scent before messenger and shirt reach him. Commentators explained a wind carrying fragrance across distance, a divinely given perception, or the language of certainty in a prophet heart. The scene should not be reduced to a laboratory claim. It expresses a love whose senses have been trained by decades of waiting and which heaven now lets arrive ahead of the visible proof.

phrases.translation: “You may think I am senile, but I certainly sense the smell of Joseph.”
phrases.explanation: If you do not call me senile I surely find Joseph scent shows Jacob knows exactly how his hope sounds to healthier people nearby. He invites them not to file perception under age before the arriving event can judge it. The phrase protects a man who has endured their management of his grief. Hope at the edge of blindness may look irrational to practical relatives until a shirt enters the room carrying the geography of Egypt.

phrases.translation: They replied, “By Allah! You are definitely still in your old delusion.”
phrases.explanation: By Allah you are in your old error repeats the household diagnosis in a softer generation of speakers. Error can mean absorbed longing and mistaken persistence in the language used about Jacob by sons and companions. They assume memory has finally become hallucination because no messenger is visible yet. The verse preserves social embarrassment around prophetic hope, reminding readers that a true perception may spend its final minutes being patronised by people who love the seer.

phrases.translation: But when the bearer of the good news arrived, he cast the shirt over Jacob’s face, so he regained his sight.
phrases.explanation: The bearer of good news casts the shirt on his face and he returns seeing, the story most tactile fulfilment of beautiful patience. Cloth, scent, skin, and eyes all participate in restoration before father and son can embrace. The shirt does not merely prove Joseph lives. It reverses the first shirt evidence of false blood into a carrier of living authority. Scripture likes tangible grace in this family because their wounds were made through tangible fabrications.

phrases.translation: Jacob then said ˹to his children˺, “Did I not tell you that I truly know from Allah what you do not know?”
phrases.explanation: Did I not tell you I know from Allah what you do not know is gentle vindication rather than an old man victory lap. Jacob knowledge was never a full map of Egypt, prison, or the cup plan. It was confidence that Joseph dream, God mercy, and an unfinished promise made despair premature. The sentence asks the household to reinterpret years of tears. What looked like senile error was knowledge carried in a form reason could not photocopy.

phrases.translation: They begged, “O our father! Pray for the forgiveness of our sins. We have certainly been sinful.”
phrases.explanation: Our father, ask forgiveness for our sins, we were sinners repeats the confession now before the parent whose heart they wounded most after Joseph. Forgiveness is sought through Jacob prayer because his nearness to Allah and his place in the injury both matter. Public family repair requires naming sin where the false blood report once stood. They no longer call their father deluded for remembering. Memory has become the witness that makes apology possible.

phrases.translation: He said, “I will pray to my Lord for your forgiveness.
phrases.explanation: I will ask my Lord forgiveness for you delays the prayer in wording later explained through seeking a blessed time such as night or dawn, although the verse leaves scheduling behind the promise. Jacob does not withhold intercession as punishment. He commits to carry their names upward as he carried Joseph absence for decades. A father prayer can become another shirt laid over the family face, restoring moral sight after confession.

phrases.translation: He ˹alone˺ is indeed the All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”
phrases.explanation: He is Forgiving and Merciful gives the sons a future wider than being permanently cast as villains in their own house. Jacob speaks the names Joseph had used when he forgave them, so heaven language circulates through the reunion. The family is learning to name God accurately at the site of its worst deed. Mercy does not rewrite the pit as harmless. It prevents the pit from remaining the last room where brothers meet.

phrases.translation: When they entered Joseph’s presence, he received his parents ˹graciously˺ and said, “Enter Egypt, Allah willing, in security.”
phrases.explanation: When they enter on Joseph he takes his parents to himself and invites them to enter Egypt in safety if Allah wills. Parents in early discussion may mean father and mother or father and an aunt standing in a mother place after Rachel death. The emotional fact is secure, because the lost child becomes host and protector to the household that lost him. Safety replaces the road, the well, the market, and the prison as governing atmosphere.

phrases.translation: Then he raised his parents to the throne, and they all fell down in prostration to Joseph, who then said, “O my dear father!
phrases.explanation: He raises his parents on the throne or couch and they fall prostrate to him completes the childhood dream through a greeting of honour suited to their time. Commentators emphasize this was not prostration of worship, which belongs only to Allah, but a courtly bowing whose permissibility belonged to earlier law or custom. Eleven brothers and parental figures align with stars, sun, and moon. The geography of a palace has become the sky a child once saw asleep.

phrases.translation: This is the interpretation of my old dream. My Lord has made it come true.
phrases.explanation: This is the interpretation of my dream from before, my Lord has made it true interprets decades of pain through fulfilment without calling every wound good in itself. A dream interpretation needs a whole biography before its grammar becomes visible. Joseph addresses his father first because Jacob guarded the dream when it was only three kinds of light and a child voice. Two generations of patience now stand inside the same recognition.

phrases.translation: He was truly kind to me when He freed me from prison,
phrases.explanation: He was kind to me when He brought me out of prison selects prison rather than the pit in Joseph public gratitude speech. The choice is often read as tact, sparing brothers a fresh naming of their crime at the reunion table. More deeply, prison was the last locked room before honour, so kindness is seen in ending the unjust confinement. Mercy in speech completes mercy in action because the wronged person controls which old doorway to reopen.

phrases.translation: and brought you all from the desert after Satan had ignited rivalry between me and my siblings.
phrases.explanation: And brought you from the desert after Satan sowed discord between me and my brothers attributes the rupture to Satan provocation without erasing their confessed sin. Desert can name their nomadic or rural life compared with Egypt settled court. Joseph language gathers the family journey as a divine kindness to all of them. He refuses to divide the final scene into his rescue and their migration. One grace has carried the house into safety.

phrases.translation: Indeed my Lord is subtle in fulfilling what He wills.
phrases.explanation: My Lord is subtle toward what He wills names the hidden fineness of providence through buckets, shirts, forgotten prisoners, dreams, and grain policy. Subtleness means God purposes travel through details too small or painful for participants to read while inside them. It is not trickery for amusement. It is gentle management by a knowledge that can use a well without approving the brothers who chose it.

phrases.translation: Surely He ˹alone˺ is the All-Knowing, All-Wise.”
phrases.explanation: All Knowing and All Wise close the long family interpretation with the names Jacob used at the dream beginning. Knowledge saw the child in the pit, the silent prisoner, and the old father at the same distance. Wisdom arranged delay so famine relief, repentance, legal vindication, and reunion matured together. The ring of the story shuts softly because the attributes that announced the promise are the attributes now praised for keeping it.

phrases.translation: “My Lord! You have surely granted me authority and taught me the interpretation of dreams.
phrases.explanation: My Lord, You gave me sovereignty and taught me interpretation turns success into inventory of gifts before any claim of self making can grow. Sovereignty here can mean his Egyptian authority, real yet borrowed and temporary. Interpretation has been the thread from childhood bed to royal court. By naming both as received, Joseph protects the summit from becoming a new pit where pride could throw away the meaning of endurance.

phrases.translation: ˹O˺ Originator of the heavens and the earth! You are my Guardian in this world and the Hereafter.
phrases.explanation: Originator of heavens and earth, You are my guardian in this world and the Hereafter expands his address beyond Egypt administration to cosmic creation. Guardian means the ally, manager, and protector who remained when family, master, prison officials, and king each changed rank around him. Naming both worlds prevents a throne from narrowing his trust. The same Lord who guarded a child in a well must now guard a ruler from the subtler dangers of honour.

phrases.translation: Allow me to die as one who submits and join me with the righteous.”
phrases.explanation: Let me die in submission and join me with the righteous is a prayer for a faithful ending, not a wish to discard present life in despair. After reunion there is still one journey greater than Canaan to Egypt. Joseph asks that office never separate him from the company of righteous servants. A story that reached its dream can still end in desire because Paradise outlasts throne, family embrace, and even fulfilled prophecy.

phrases.translation: That is from the stories of the unseen which We reveal to you ˹O Prophet˺.
phrases.explanation: That is from the reports of the unseen revealed to you returns the listening frame to Muhammad after Joseph prayer. Domestic dialogue in wells, bedrooms, prisons, and family councils could not have come from being an eyewitness. The story is offered as known through revelation while its lessons remain available to every audience. As with Noah in the previous chapter, hidden scenes become credentials and consolation in one.

phrases.translation: You were not present when they ˹all˺ made up their minds, and when they plotted ˹against Joseph˺
phrases.explanation: You were not with them when they agreed and plotted seals the point at the story earliest secret. The brothers plan was hidden even inside its own time except to God and the child who survived it. Muhammad absence from that meeting emphasises revealed knowledge without challenging hearers to produce a competing archive. A plot designed to erase a witness has been narrated centuries later by the Lord who watched the hands close over the well.

phrases.translation: And most people will not believe—no matter how keen you are—
phrases.explanation: Most people will not believe however eager you are gives the Prophet the same release Joseph father received across long delay. Teacher longing cannot convert a whole audience by intensity alone. The sentence is a protection against measuring truth by majority response in a single season. Joseph was followed first by a few prisoners and remembered later by one cupbearer. Revelation can be alive in the world long before society appears ready.

phrases.translation: even though you are not asking them for a reward for this ˹Quran˺.
phrases.explanation: You do not ask them a wage for it removes salesmanship from Muhammad mission as it did from Noah, Hud, and Joseph scenes. A free message cannot be accused honestly of needing customer satisfaction to survive. The audience may reject a gift, yet refusal says more about the receiver scale than the giver motive. In a chapter filled with prices, coins, measures, and stores, revelation is the one priceless provision offered without a market stall.

phrases.translation: It is only a reminder to the whole world
phrases.explanation: It is only a reminder for the worlds gives the story an audience beyond Arabs, Egyptians, Israelites, and one generation of hearers. A reminder awakens what fitful conscience already suspects about envy, patience, chastity, and providence. Worlds can include humans across time and place whose family situations never involve a throne. Joseph biography becomes an address system through which ordinary readers find their own pit, prison, temptation, or brother.

phrases.translation: How many signs in the heavens and the earth do they pass by with indifference
phrases.explanation: How many signs in heavens and earth they pass by while turning away broadens the indictment beyond refusal of one book. Stars that opened Joseph dream, seasons that governed famine, roads and ruins all speak in public. Turning away is a bodily direction that can become an intellectual habit. The verse asks whether a person can be surrounded by evidence and still be information poor because attention has been trained to leave.

phrases.translation: And most of them do not believe in Allah without associating others with Him ˹in worship˺
phrases.explanation: Most of them do not believe in Allah without associating others captures mixed religion rather than simple atheism. A person can affirm the Creator while distributing ultimate fear, hope, law, and worship among ancestors, saints, idols, or powers. Joseph prison sermon already supplied the distinction. The danger is a divided sky where Allah is praised as highest and then edited by smaller sovereigns whenever appetite needs permission.

phrases.translation: Do they feel secure that an overwhelming torment from Allah will not overtake them,
phrases.explanation: Do they feel secure from an overwhelming punishment of Allah coming to them draws complacency into the light after signs have been passed. Security is treated as a feeling that can be false even while walls stand. The nations in the previous chapter felt locally secure in cliffs, markets, and courts. This question asks present hearers to check whether routine has become an argument against judgment simply because yesterday ended quietly.

phrases.translation: or that the Hour will not take them by surprise when they least expect ˹it˺
phrases.explanation: Or the Hour arriving suddenly while they do not perceive makes final time an interruption rather than a public countdown. Joseph story also turned on sudden arrivals, a bucket, a king dream, a cup discovery, and a scent before a caravan. Divine timing often catches people in ordinary posture. The verse does not create panic about every hour. It removes the assumed right to schedule repentance after every visible task has been completed.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “This is my way. I invite to Allah with insight—I and those who follow me.
phrases.explanation: This is my way, I call to Allah on clear sight defines prophetic work after the story lessons have been gathered. Clear sight can mean insight, evidence, and certainty, so invitation is not imitation of family custom for a better tribe. Those who follow Muhammad share the road and method rather than merely the label. A caller with sight can resist both market editing and angry despair when a majority still turns away.

phrases.translation: Glory be to Allah, and I am not one of the polytheists.”
phrases.explanation: Glory be to Allah and I am not among the associators separates the way from every mixed sovereignty criticised in the previous verses. The declaration is simple because the entire Joseph narrative has shown what divided loyalties do to households, courts, prisons, and markets. Not being an associator is stated as identity rather than a debating trick. A story about one family ends with the Prophet publicly choosing the one direction his life will keep facing.

phrases.translation: We only sent before you ˹O Prophet˺ men inspired by Us from among the people of each society.
phrases.explanation: Before you We sent only men from town communities to whom We revealed returns to the humanity of messengers that Noah and Joseph audiences resisted. Men from settlements speak local languages and know roads, markets, hunger, marriage, and courts. Their ordinariness is pedagogical rather than accidental. A guide who needs food and family can be imitated in patience and conduct in ways an angel visitor might not require from ordinary people.

phrases.translation: Have the deniers not travelled through the land to see what was the end of those ˹destroyed˺ before them?
phrases.explanation: Have they not travelled and seen the end of those before them asks deniers to let geography tutor conscience. Trade roads already carry travellers past empty houses, broken cisterns, and named ruins that merchants can point to between markets. Seeing an end is different from collecting curiosities because the traveller must imagine a living society inside the absent noise. The question gathers the preceding chapter of towns into the feet of the present audience.

phrases.translation: And surely the ˹eternal˺ Home of the Hereafter is far better for those mindful ˹of Allah˺. Will you not then understand
phrases.explanation: The home of the Hereafter is better for the mindful while will you not reason closes the travel argument with a scale larger than archaeology. Ruins can teach that earthly homes end, yet faith supplies another home where endurance is not reduced to an epitaph. Reasoning here means drawing the practical conclusion before one address joins the tour. Mindful people leave a ruin carrying repentance rather than only a story to retell.

phrases.translation: And when the messengers despaired and their people thought the messengers had been denied help, Our help came to them ˹at last˺.
phrases.explanation: Until messengers despaired and thought they had been denied or were belied is one of the most delicate verses about prophetic delay. Readings and commentators differ over the exact subject and sense of being told lies or having help assumed impossible. The shared scene is extreme length, where human endurance reaches a point at which rescue no longer looks visible by ordinary means. Joseph forgotten prison years give the sentence an immediate face.

phrases.translation: We then saved whoever We willed, and Our punishment is never averted from the wicked people
phrases.explanation: Our help came and who We willed was saved makes rescue arrive from beyond the exhausted timetable rather than as payment for never feeling strain. Punishment not turned from guilty people balances the promise so delay does not become universal amnesty. The verse consoles Muhammad with a history in which heaven often waits until storytellers think the thread is lost. Divine help can be late by a prophet calendar and exact by God appointment.

phrases.translation: In their stories there is truly a lesson for people of reason.
phrases.explanation: In their stories is a lesson for people of intelligence returns to the opening claim with a more demanding word for deep minds. Intelligence here is the inner core that can move from one family to universal patterns without stripping away particulars. A casual listener can enjoy recognition scenes. A person of understanding asks where envy starts, how providence works through means, when forgiveness becomes possible, and why power must remain a trust.

phrases.translation: This message cannot be a fabrication, rather ˹it is˺ a confirmation of previous revelation,
phrases.explanation: It is not a fabricated tale but confirmation of what was before it places the Quran in continuity with earlier revelation while refusing human manufacture. The Joseph account can resonate with older sacred memory and still claim its own revealed form. Confirmation does not mean every later community retelling is endorsed in every detail. It means the central prophetic history is not being invented in isolation by its Arabian reciter.

phrases.translation: a detailed explanation of all things, a guide, and a mercy for people of faith
phrases.explanation: Detailed explanation of all things, guidance, and mercy for believing people gives the final inventory of the Book after the best of stories. Detail can mean principles needed for faith and life rather than an encyclopedia of every object. Guidance shows a road, while mercy describes how the road feels to people wounded by pits and prisons. The chapter ends by promising that a story understood in faith becomes care for the reader.
